bib.title: Spectral Normalization for Generative Adversarial Networks

question: Can constraining the spectral norm of each discriminator layer stabilize GAN training more cheaply and robustly than weight clipping, weight normalization, orthonormal regularization or gradient penalty?
hypothesis: Normalizing each weight matrix by its largest singular value bounds the discriminator's Lipschitz constant without collapsing the rank of the weights, so training is more robust to hyperparameters and the generator is more diverse.
contributions: Spectral normalization: divide each discriminator weight matrix by its largest singular value, estimated with one power-iteration step per update.
Analysis showing weight normalization, Frobenius normalization and weight clipping favour low-rank weight matrices while spectral normalization does not.
Experiments on CIFAR-10, STL-10 and ILSVRC2012 (ImageNet) comparing against seven alternative regularisers across six optimizer settings.

method.summary: Each discriminator weight matrix W is replaced by W/sigma(W), where sigma(W) is estimated with a single power-iteration step whose vector u is reused between updates. SN-GANs are compared with weight clipping, GAN-GP, WGAN-GP, batch norm, layer norm, weight norm and orthonormal regularization on CIFAR-10 and STL-10 under six Adam settings, then scaled to conditional ImageNet generation at 128x128.
method.task: unsupervised and class-conditional image generation with GANs

models.name: SN-GAN, standard CNN
models.architecture: Generator: dense to Mg x Mg x 512, three 4x4 stride-2 deconvs with BN (256,128,64), 3x3 conv 3 Tanh. Discriminator: seven conv layers (64,64,128,128,256,256,512) with leaky ReLU slope 0.1, then dense to 1. Mg=4 for CIFAR-10, 6 for STL-10.

models.name: SN-GAN, ResNet
models.architecture: ResNet generator and discriminator after Gulrajani et al. 2017 (Tables 4-6); no BN in discriminator ResBlocks, global sum pooling; ImageNet generator uses conditional batch norm, conditional D concatenates a 128-d label embedding.

other.sn_gan_generator_feature_maps: doubled versus original for SN-GANs (Appendix B.2)

training.objective: Standard GAN loss (Eq. 15) with the alternate non-saturating generator cost; also hinge loss (Eqs. 16-17); WGAN-GP objective for that baseline; conditional ImageNet used hinge loss
training.lr: 0.0001 to 0.001 depending on setting (Table 1); 0.0002 for ResNet
training.lr_schedule: ImageNet: linear decay to 0 after 400K iterations; others not stated
training.steps: 100K generator updates for all CIFAR/STL experiments unless noted; STL-10 SN-GAN also run at 2x; ImageNet 450K generator updates
training.regularisation: Spectral normalization on every discriminator layer, one power iteration per update, u recycled between steps; baselines: weight clipping c=0.01, gradient penalty lambda=10, orthonormal regularizer ||W^T W - I||_F^2
training.wall_clock: Relative: SN-GAN about 110-120% of weight normalization time on CIFAR-10; about the same as vanilla GAN on STL-10 (Fig 10, values read from bar chart not extracted)
training.seeds: ResNet: multiple random seeds, mean and std over models; count not stated

other.batch_norm_multiplier_gamma: gamma excluded from WN, BN and LN baselines to keep Lipschitz condition
other.conv_weight_treatment: conv weight treated as 2-D matrix dout x (din*h*w)

inference.samples: Inception score: 5000 generated images per evaluation, repeated 10 times (mean and std); FID over 10000 and 5000 samples

metrics.name: FID
metrics.definition: Frechet distance between Gaussian fits of Inception features of real and generated images

metrics.name: intra MS-SSIM
metrics.definition: MS-SSIM between pairs of independently generated images of one class, as in Odena et al. 2017; measures mode collapse

eval.protocol: Six optimizer settings per method on CIFAR-10 and STL-10; best setting reported in Table 2; ImageNet compared to orthonormal regularization and AC-GAN; no significance test.

availability.weights: pretrained models available at the same repo

results.claim: With the standard CNN, SN-GAN has a higher CIFAR-10 inception score than weight clipping, WGAN-GP, BN, LN and WN, and is level with orthonormal regularization (7.42 vs 7.40).

results.claim: The spectral norm of each discriminator layer stays near 1 throughout training with a single power iteration.

results.claim: SN-GAN training costs about 110 to 120% of weight normalization time on CIFAR-10 and is much faster than WGAN-GP.
Weight clipping and weight normalization give low-rank discriminator layers (singular values concentrated on a few components) while spectral normalization gives broadly distributed singular values.

limits: Authors concede the comparison across rows of Table 2 differs in optimizer and architecture: 'all methods listed thereof are all different in both optimization methods and the architecture of the model'.
Orthonormal regularization is slightly better than SN-GAN on STL-10 with the standard CNN at equal iterations (8.56 vs 8.28) and at the best setting.

The Lipschitz bound is an upper bound; layerwise product of 1 does not make the discriminator tight, and the paper offers no theory of why it improves sample quality (future work 'on more theoretical basis').
Only Inception score and FID on 32x32 to 128x128 images; no precision/recall, no human evaluation; no number of seeds or batch size given; hardware and wall-clock in seconds are only in a bar chart.
Dated: 2018 GAN era; diffusion models have superseded GANs for most image generation, though SN is still used in GAN discriminators.
Each method is tuned over only 6 optimizer settings and the best is reported; no significance test across settings.

terms.definition: W_SN(W) := W/sigma(W), normalizing the weight matrix by its largest singular value so that sigma(W_SN)=1
For a linear layer g(h)=Wh, ||g||_Lip = sigma(W), the largest singular value

lineage.work: Spectral norm regularization for improving the generalizability of deep learning

Squared singular values of weight matrices trained with different methods: Weight clipping (WC), Weight Normalization (WN) and Spectral Normalization (SN).
figures.why: Shows rank collapse under WC and WN versus broad spectrum under SN; the central mechanism.

figures.caption: Computational time for 100 updates. We set ndis = 5

figures.caption: Visualization of the difference between spectral normalization (Red) and weight normalization (Blue) on possible sets of singular values.

code.snippet: v <- W^T u / ||W^T u||_2 ; u <- W v / ||W v||_2 ; sigma(W) ~= u^T W v ; W_SN = W / sigma(W)
